authority_behaviour: rec_layer_s3.c:612-944: the record reader returns the body length and the buffer contains exactly those bytes; alert decoding reads only that body.
A short BIO read is a retry; the partial header/body is retained (rec_layer_s3.c:161-...).
Message-layer framing is type(1)||length(3)||body; a message split across records is assembled; ChangeCipherSpec (20) is skipped.
A length that exceeds the record buffer is a fatal record overflow (rec_layer_s3.c:669-672).

boundaries.operation: received-record delivery into caller-supplied writable memory
boundaries.before: A &mut [u8] over the whole caller capacity was formed before any byte was written; the alert decoder was handed &out[..n] through that slice.
boundaries.after: The buffer stays a raw writable region. Plaintext and non-AEAD arms copy with core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping after a body.len() <= cap check; the decrypt arms pass the raw pointer and capacity. A &[u8] is published only over the prefix ssl3_read_one_record reports written (n <= cap), and an n == 0 alert takes an empty slice rather than deriving one from a possibly-NULL buffer.
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED: typed-slice construction over uninitialised caller memory. RETAINED: the C ABI writes into caller memory through a raw pointer with an explicit SAFETY contract.

boundaries.operation: handshake-message delivery into caller-supplied writable memory
boundaries.before: &mut [u8] over cap, then dst.copy_from_slice(msg). statem_srvr::tls13_server_drive supplies OwnedBuf::new memory, which is CRYPTO_malloc and therefore uninitialised: real UB on the TLS1.3 server path.
boundaries.after: msg_len > cap returns -1 with rd_msg_off unchanged; otherwise core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping writes exactly msg_len bytes. rd_msg_off advances only after the copy, so a refusal leaves the assembled message reusable.
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED: typed slice over uninitialised heap output. RETAINED: the raw copy with an explicit non-overlap/initialised-source contract.

boundaries.operation: authenticated-plaintext publication to the record layer's output buffer
boundaries.before: &mut [u8] over out_cap was formed after authentication, then out[..content_len].copy_from_slice.
boundaries.after: Both sinks check content_len <= out_cap and write with core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping from the cleansed plaintext block; they never read out. Authentication and cleansing semantics are unchanged.
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED: two more whole-capacity typed slices. RETAINED: the raw copy, with a contract that out may be uninitialised.
boundaries.state: IMPLEMENTED + FAST-tested (author). These two files are the sink of the rec_layer boundary; no other change was made to them.

in_place_case_proof.same_allocation: There is no input/output same-allocation case on this path. Input is rec_body/rec_hdr (fields of Ssl) or the cleansed plaintext block; output is rx_buf (a different Ssl field), rd_msg_buf (different field, written only by the internal ssl3_read_bytes call), an application-owned OwnedBuf/vec, or a stack local.
in_place_case_proof.initialised_input: rec_body[:len] is initialised by BIO_read (len <= 17000), rec_hdr is zero-initialised then filled, rd_msg_buf[:rd_msg_len] is written by the record reader, and the plaintext block is initialised by EVP_DecryptUpdate/Final before the copy.
in_place_case_proof.no_overlapping_mut_borrows: The mutable borrow of rd_msg_buf used to obtain dst_ptr ends before ssl3_read_bytes is called (block-scoped). No &mut to the caller's output is ever created; only raw copies touch it. The decrypted plaintext lives in a separate OwnedBuf allocation. The only read-back is the alert prefix, written by the immediately preceding ssl3_read_one_record.
in_place_case_proof.caller_inventory_shows_non_overlap: Every caller enumerated above passes a buffer distinct from rec_hdr/rec_body/rd_msg_buf. This is now a documented # Safety precondition on all three entry points rather than an implied assumption.

unsafe_ops.before_after: rec_layer_s3.rs total `unsafe {` blocks 73 -> 78 (production 58 -> 59; #[cfg(test)] 15 -> 19). t1_enc.rs 34 -> 34 and tls13_enc.rs 84 -> 84 (the copies replace a block one-for-one inside the existing function-level unsafe block).
unsafe_ops.removed: 5 typed-slice constructions over caller output (3 in rec_layer_s3.rs, 2 in the decrypt sinks).
unsafe_ops.introduced: Production: 2 core::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping blocks in ssl3_read_one_record, 1 core::slice::from_raw_parts over the written alert prefix, 1 `&[]` alert call for the n == 0 arm, and 1 copy inside tls13_next_handshake_message's existing unsafe block. Each has a SAFETY comment; the copies are write-only and length-bounded by cap.
unsafe_ops.net: The three defect-carrying from_raw_parts_mut calls in the target file are gone (0 remain over caller capacity). No exported symbol, layout or seam constant changed.

discharged: Caller output is never read before it is written; the published extent is exactly the returned n.
The alert decoder receives only initialised bytes (n == 0 uses an empty slice).
Non-overlap of output with the connection's record/assembly buffers is stated as a caller precondition and established by the caller inventory.
The decrypt sinks write only content_len <= out_cap bytes and never read the output.
retained: The C ABI still hands raw writable memory: validity of the pointer/extent is a boundary precondition, documented per function.
A caller that passes a buffer overlapping rec_body/rd_msg_buf would still violate the contract (no current caller does; not enforceable in the type system at this ABI).

compatibility_delta: No behaviour change intended. Short reads, retry/rwstate, record-overflow poisoning, alert outcomes and fragmented reassembly are untouched; the only changed operations are slice construction and copy. All 17 rec_layer tests (including the 12 pre-existing boundary tests) pass, plus the 8 ssl::t1_enc and 16 ssl::tls13_enc AEAD round-trip/refusal tests. Divergences recorded: none (AGENTS.md section 17: no authority behaviour reproduced or corrected).
